requirements.text: Include caching hints (ttlMs, cacheScope) on results with resultType: 'complete' returned by server/discover, tools/list, prompts/list, resources/list, resources/templates/list, resources/read.
Cacheable hints are NOT present on interim results with resultType: 'input_required' (MRTR pattern) — these are not cacheable.
Serve a cached response for a request whose method or parameters (that affect the result, e.g. uri for resources/read, cursor for paginated list requests) differ from the request that produced it.

Cache results produced by retrying a request via the multi round-trip requests (MRTR) mechanism, i.e. requests carrying inputResponses or requestState, since they depend on inputs outside the cache key.
Consider a result with ttlMs=0 immediately stale and re-fetch every time the result is needed.
If ttlMs is positive, consider the result fresh for that many ms after receiving the response.
If ttlMs is absent (older server versions only), assume default of 0 (immediately stale) and rely on own heuristics/notifications.
If ttlMs is negative, ignore it and treat as 0.
Provide a ttlMs value that is >= 0.
Compute freshness as: now < t_received + ttlMs, where t_received is local time response was received; once expired, treat as stale and re-fetch on next access.
Treat TTL as a polling interval triggering automatic background refetches; TTL is a freshness hint checked only on access.
If implementing background polling anyway, apply jitter and backoff.
Re-fetch before TTL expires if there is reason to believe data changed (e.g., an unexpected 'method not found' or 'invalid params' error on a related call).
Serve stale responses if errors occur during re-fetch (network issues, server downtime).
For cacheScope 'public', any client, shared gateway, or caching proxy may store and serve the cached response to any user, even across different authorization contexts/access tokens.
requirements.cite: caching.md table lines 100-103; Security Considerations lines 175

requirements.text: For cacheScope 'private', reuse cached responses for the same authorization context only.
Share 'private'-scoped caches across authorization contexts (a different access token requires a different cache).
Ensure cacheScope correctly reflects the intended visibility of the primitive.
Apply appropriate per-primitive access controls; MUST NOT rely on cacheScope alone to prevent unauthorized access to primitives.
Provide ttlMs without advertising listChanged: true (client then relies entirely on TTL-based freshness).
Advertise listChanged: true AND provide ttlMs — client uses TTL to avoid refetches between notifications; the notification acts as immediate invalidation.
When a relevant change notification is received while a cached response is still fresh, treat the notification as invalidating the cached response immediately (considered immediately stale).
requirements.cite: caching.md lines 122-123 (normative prose: 'the notification invalidates the cached response')

requirements.text: Each paginated page is independently cacheable; freshness clock for each page starts when that page was received.
Return different ttlMs values on different pages of the same list (e.g. longer TTL for early/stable pages, shorter for the final page).
Re-fetch an expired cached page using its cursor.

Re-fetch from the beginning (without a cursor) if a consistent snapshot of the full list is required, since there is no cross-page consistency guarantee (data changes between fetches may cause duplicates or gaps).
If a cursor becomes invalid (server returns an error for a previously valid cursor), discard all cached pages and re-fetch from the beginning.
Apply the same cacheScope to all response pages for a given list request (e.g., if page 1 of tools/list is 'private', all subsequent pages for that request MUST also be 'private').
Not assume a fixed page size; page size is server-determined.

Treat cursors as opaque tokens: don't assume format, don't parse/modify, and don't make any determination based on cursor value other than whether a non-null value was provided — an empty string is a valid cursor and MUST NOT be treated as end-of-results.
Provide stable cursors and handle invalid cursors gracefully.
Treat a missing nextCursor as the end of results, and support both paginated and non-paginated flows.
Invalid cursors SHOULD result in an error with JSON-RPC code -32602 (Invalid params).

Every request MUST include required _meta fields: io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion, io.modelcontextprotocol/clientInfo, io.modelcontextprotocol/clientCapabilities (per basic/index#meta; omitted from pagination.md examples for brevity).
Include resultType field on results for protocol version 2026-07-28.
When receiving a result from a server on an earlier protocol version that omits resultType, treat the absent field as 'complete' (backward compatibility).

wire_details: _meta keys referenced (pagination.md line 19-20): io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion, io.modelcontextprotocol/clientInfo, io.modelcontextprotocol/clientCapabilities — required on every request per basic/index#meta (not detailed further in the two focus files).
JSON-RPC error code -32602 = Invalid params, used (SHOULD) for invalid cursor errors (pagination.md line 113).
Field name: cursor (string, request param) — schema.ts PaginatedRequestParams.cursor?: Cursor; type Cursor = string (schema.ts line 172).
Field name: nextCursor (string, optional, response) — schema.ts PaginatedResult.nextCursor?: Cursor.
Field name: ttlMs (integer milliseconds, required on CacheableResult, minimum 0) — schema.ts CacheableResult.ttlMs: number, @minimum 0.
Field name: cacheScope (required on CacheableResult) — enum exactly "public" | "private" — schema.ts CacheableResult.cacheScope.
Field name: resultType — type ResultType = "complete" | "input_required" | string (open string union, schema.ts line 216); Result.resultType is required per 2026-07-28 (schema.ts line 234).

Example JSON response shape (pagination.md lines 41-53): {jsonrpc:'2.0', id, result:{resultType:'complete', resources:[...], nextCursor:'<opaque base64-like string, e.g. eyJwYWdlIjogM30=>', ttlMs:300000, cacheScope:'public'}}.
Example request with cursor (pagination.md lines 60-69): {jsonrpc:'2.0', id, method:'resources/list', params:{cursor:'<opaque string>'}}.

resultType values enumerated by spec: 'complete' (final content) and 'input_required' (MRTR — carries an InputRequiredResult object with instructions, referenced from schema.ts comment at line 213, detailed in mrtr pattern doc not read here).

No HTTP-transport-specific header names appear in caching.md or pagination.md (analogies to HTTP Cache-Control: max-age / public / private are semantic analogies only, not actual transport headers) — MCP's ttlMs/cacheScope are JSON body fields on the Result object, not HTTP headers.

PaginatedRequestParams extends RequestParams (schema.ts line 1054) — RequestParams presumably carries its own _meta (RequestParams not fully expanded in excerpts read, but Notification/Result pattern shows _meta: XMetaObject conventions).

CacheableResult and PaginatedResult are both marked @internal / mixin interfaces in schema.ts — concrete results compose via 'extends PaginatedResult, CacheableResult' (e.g. ListResourcesResult, ListResourceTemplatesResult, ListPromptsResult, ListToolsResult) or CacheableResult alone (DiscoverResult, ReadResourceResult).
sdk_implications: PowerShell SDK must model a shared base type (e.g. an interface/abstract class or trait applied via composition, since PowerShell/.NET lacks multiple inheritance for classes) implementing CacheableResult: required int64/int property TtlMs (>=0, validated on serialization) and required enum property CacheScope with only 'public'|'private' — serialize/deserialize exactly these two lowercase string literals.

Separately model PaginatedResult mixin: optional string NextCursor. Because .NET classes are single-inheritance, use interfaces (ICacheableResult, IPaginatedResult) or composition, and have ListResourcesResult, ListResourceTemplatesResult, ListPromptsResult, ListToolsResult implement BOTH; DiscoverResult and ReadResourceResult implement CacheableResult only (not paginated).

Client-side cache implementation must key cache entries by (method, uri) for resources/read and by (method, cursor) for the four list methods — implement as a composite key/dictionary, not just method name.

Client must implement TTL freshness check using local received-time timestamp: store t_received (DateTimeOffset.UtcNow) per cache entry; freshness predicate: DateTimeOffset.UtcNow < t_received + TimeSpan.FromMilliseconds(ttlMs). Must clamp ttlMs<0 to 0 and treat missing ttlMs as 0.

Client must implement cacheScope partitioning: private-scope cache store keyed additionally by the active auth/access-token/authorization-context identifier; public-scope cache store shared globally regardless of caller identity.

Client must implement invalidation-on-notification: subscribe to notifications/tools/list_changed, notifications/prompts/list_changed, notifications/resources/list_changed (and resource updated notifications) to purge matching cache entries immediately, independent of TTL.
Client cache MUST bypass/never store results whose request included inputResponses or requestState (MRTR retry params) — implement a pre-cache guard that checks these params before writing to cache.
Client cache MUST bypass/never store results whose resultType != 'complete' (i.e. resultType === 'input_required' results are never cached).

Cursor type must be represented as an opaque string (do not attempt to Base64-decode, parse, or interpret it); pagination helper (e.g. Get-McpAllPages / IAsyncEnumerable-based enumerator) must treat empty string '' as a valid continuation cursor distinct from null/absent, i.e. use nullable-string semantics ($null vs '') not falsy-string checks.
Auto-pagination helper cmdlets should stop when nextCursor is absent (null), not when it's falsy/empty, and should support resuming with an arbitrary opaque cursor string supplied by the caller.

Server-side SDK helper for building paginated+cacheable responses should require callers to supply ttlMs and cacheScope for tools/list, prompts/list, resources/list, resources/templates/list, resources/read, and server/discover results; consider throwing/validating if ttlMs < 0 before serialization.
Server-side SDK must throw/return JSON-RPC error -32602 (Invalid params) when an unrecognized/invalid cursor is supplied to a paginated list handler.

Server-side pagination helper must guarantee cacheScope consistency across pages of the same logical list request (track and reuse the scope decided for page 1 across subsequent cursor-driven pages of that same request).
SDK should implement backward-compatibility shim: if resultType is absent in a deserialized Result (older server), default to 'complete' rather than throwing a deserialization error.
SDK should NOT implement TTL-based background polling by default; if an optional polling feature is added, it must apply jitter+backoff per spec.

resultType field (with 'complete'|'input_required'|string) and the whole multi-round-trip-request (MRTR) pattern are new/changed in 2026-07-28; backward-compat rule requires clients to treat an absent resultType from older servers as 'complete'.

Pagination model itself (opaque cursor, nextCursor, four list operations, -32602 for invalid cursor) appears unchanged in substance from prior revisions based on the pagination.md content read; the only new interaction is pagination.md's explicit tie-in with the new caching model (each page independently cacheable, cacheScope must be consistent across pages) — this cross-cutting rule is new for 2026-07-28.

summary: 2026-07-28 introduces a caching layer (ttlMs, cacheScope) on top of the pre-existing opaque cursor-based pagination model. Six operations MUST carry caching hints when resultType:'complete': server/discover, tools/list, prompts/list, resources/list, resources/templates/list, resources/read; interim resultType:'input_required' (MRTR) results are never cacheable, nor are MRTR retries (requests with inputResponses/requestState). CacheableResult requires ttlMs (integer ms, >=0, HTTP max-age-like semantics; 0/negative/absent all resolve to "immediately stale") and cacheScope ("public"|"private", HTTP Cache-Control public/private analogy; private caches MUST NOT cross authorization contexts). Cache key = method + result-affecting params (uri for resources/read, cursor for list ops). Notifications (listChanged) complement TTL and immediately invalidate fresh cache entries. Four of the six operations (all list ops except resources/read and server/discover) also support pagination via opaque string Cursor: request.params.cursor optional, response.nextCursor optional signals more pages; clients MUST treat cursors as opaque (empty string is a valid, non-terminal cursor) and MUST NOT assume fixed page size; invalid cursors SHOULD produce JSON-RPC -32602. Pagination and caching interact: each page is independently cacheable with its own ttlMs (which MAY differ per page), but cacheScope MUST be identical across all pages of one list request; no cross-page consistency is guaranteed, and clients needing a consistent snapshot SHOULD restart pagination from the beginning. Result.resultType is now a required field (open string enum 'complete'|'input_required'|string), with mandatory backward-compat fallback to 'complete' when absent from older servers.
